recognize_zh: 箭頭所指的紅血球略帶藍灰色（多染性），細胞質內有一條細長、沿著細胞邊緣內側繞行的紫色環狀細線，這就是 Cabot 環（Cabot ring）；周邊另可見一個淚滴狀紅血球。
features: Single slightly polychromatic red cell (arrow) containing a thin, reddish-violet, circular ring lying just inside the cell membrane
Ring is threadlike and continuous, without a central dot or granular beading
Background red cells are mostly normochromic with little central pallor; mild anisocytosis
Occasional poikilocyte including a teardrop cell (lower right)
No Howell-Jolly body or leukocytes in this field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear at high power shows red cells with mild anisocytosis and occasional poikilocytes, including a teardrop cell. One slightly polychromatic red cell contains a thin, circular, violet-staining ring inclusion paralleling the cell membrane, characteristic of a Cabot ring. No Howell-Jolly body, parasites, or nucleated red cells are seen in this field. Findings are consistent with a Cabot ring, a marker of disordered or stressed erythropoiesis such as severe hemolytic or megaloblastic anemia.

ddx.vs: A malaria ring trophozoite is small (about one-third of the cell) with a discrete blue cytoplasmic ring and a red chromatin dot, whereas a Cabot ring is a thin, dot-less thread tracing the full cell periphery.
Babesia forms are small intraerythrocytic rings or tetrads with chromatin dots and no pigment, not a single membrane-hugging thread.
Drying artifact is refractile and changes with focus, while a Cabot ring stains violet and remains in focus as a true inclusion.
